title: New York Sales Tax Guide: Rates & Compliance
summary: This guide explains New York's sales tax rates and requirements in simple terms to help you file correctly and avoid penalties.
body_markdown:
## New York sales tax at a glance


State taxing authority New York Department of Taxation and Finance


New York sales tax rate 4%


Local tax rates 3% to 4.875%


Combined sales tax rate range based on state tax rate plus local tax rate 7% to 8.875%


Economic nexus threshold More than $500,000 in gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property and more than 100 such sales in the preceding four sales tax quarters


Website[tax.ny.gov](https://www.tax.ny.gov/)


Tax line(518) 485-2889


New York State has a 4% base sales tax rate, but cities and counties add their own local taxes. In New York City and seven surrounding counties, buyers pay an additional 0.375% tax for the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District (MCTD).


This means a business owner will charge a combined rate between 7% and 8.875%, depending on the delivery address. A buyer in Glens Falls will pay 7%, while a buyer in New York City will pay 8.875% because of additional local taxes, including the MCTD tax.


This sales tax applies to most[tangible personal property and certain services](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/st/subject.htm) , like utilities and telephone service. Some tangible personal property may be exempt from sales tax, but local tax jurisdictions can opt out of exempting items.


Business owners should check if they meet the requirements for[economic nexus in New York](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/new-york) . In the preceding four sales tax quarters, you must have more than $500,000 in gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property delivered into New York and more than 100 such sales.


Before you charge New York sales tax, you must register for a[NY.gov business account](https://www.tax.ny.gov/online/bus.htm) and[register as a vendor](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/st/register.htm) .


When you’re calculating sales tax rates for your customers, you’ll base the rate on the address where the customer takes delivery. To ensure that you’re using the most accurate rate, look up the delivery address on the state’s[Jurisdiction/Rate Lookup by Address tool](https://www8.tax.ny.gov/JRLA/jrlaStart) .

## New York sales tax rates and calculations


New Yorkers can expect to pay between 7% and 8.875% in sales tax. This includes a 4% base sales tax rate.[Each tax jurisdiction](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/publications/sales/pub718.pdf) applies its own local taxes that range from 3% to 4.875%. The MCTD tax of 0.375% applies in the five New York City boroughs and seven surrounding counties.


### List of local sales tax rates in New York


A zip code or city name isn’t enough information to ensure you’re charging the correct sales tax rate. Use New York’s[Jurisdiction/Rate Lookup by Address tool](https://www8.tax.ny.gov/JRLA/jrlaStart) before applying a rate to a sale.


City County/Borough Base State Rate Local Rate MCTD Combined Rate


**Albany** Albany 4% 4% N/A 8%


**Buffalo** Erie 4% 4.75% N/A 8.75%


**Mount Vernon** Westchester 4% 4% 0.375% 8.375%


**New Rochelle** Westchester 4% 4% 0.375% 8.375%


**New York City** Bronx, Kings, New York, Queens, Richmond 4% 4.5% 0.375% 8.875%


**Rochester** Monroe 4% 4% N/A 8%


**Schenectady** Schenectady 4% 4% N/A 8%


**Syracuse** Onondaga 4% 4% N/A 8%


**Utica** Oneida 4% 4.75% N/A 8.75%


**Yonkers** Westchester 4% 4.5% 0.375% 8.875%


### How to calculate New York sales tax


To calculate the amount of sales tax you should charge, you add the base rate of 4% and the local tax rate together. Then, multiply the sales tax rate by the purchase price to get the total amount of sales tax to charge.


For example, a buyer in Utica purchases an item for $50. You add the 4% base rate to the 4.75% local tax to get 8.75%. Then, multiply 8.75% by $50, which equals $4.375. Round up to $4.38.


### Origin vs. destination sourcing in New York


New York uses destination-based sourcing. That means tax is calculated based on where the buyer receives the product, not where the seller is located.


### Is New York a Streamlined Sales Tax state?


No, New York is not a[Streamlined Member State](https://www.streamlinedsalestax.org/state-details/new-york) .


## Sales tax nexus in New York


[Nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-nexus) refers to the connection between a business and a state. A business has[physical nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) if it has an office, warehouse, employee, or inventory in that state.[Economic nexus](https://www.numeral.com/blog/economic-nexus) means an out-of-state business meets the requirements for charging sales tax to customers in that state.


There are two other types of nexus that can sometimes apply. Affiliate nexus means a business has a connection with an affiliated company or representative that operates in that state. That can create nexus for an out-of-state company.


Click-through nexus occurs when a New York resident or business refers customers through website or affiliate links.


Before 2018, states couldn’t require out-of-state sellers to charge the state sales tax on online purchases. In[South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc.](https://www.numeral.com/blog/south-dakota-v-wayfair) , the U.S. Supreme Court overturned that precedent, and states with a sales tax began setting economic nexus thresholds.


The[economic threshold in NY](https://www.numeral.com/nexus/new-york) is both a certain number of transactions and a dollar amount in sales. Numeral makes it easy to determine whether you meet the nexus threshold with[free nexus monitoring](https://www.numeral.com/product/nexus-tracking) .


Nexus Type Threshold


**Physical** Any[physical presence](https://www.numeral.com/blog/physical-nexus) in New York, such as an office, warehouse, employees, or inventory


**Economic** More than $500,000 in gross receipts from sales of tangible personal property delivered into New York during the preceding four sales tax quarters and more than 100 sales of tangible personal property delivered into the state


**Marketplace**[Marketplace facilitators](https://www.numeral.com/blog/marketplace-facilitator) exceeding New York’s economic nexus threshold generally must collect and remit sales tax on behalf of their sellers


**Affiliate** Ties to an in-state business that helps develop, market, or facilitate sales of the retailer’s goods may create nexus, subject to a small-seller exception


## What's taxable and exempt in New York


In New York, buyers[must pay sales tax](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/tg_bulletins/st/quick_reference_guide_for_taxable_and_exempt_property_and_services.htm) on purchases of tangible personal property unless it is specifically exempt. Utilities and certain services, like gas, electricity, and phone service, are also subject to sales tax. Travelers also must pay sales tax on hotel rooms and short-term rentals. Restaurants and bars must charge sales tax on food and beverages.


Some purchases are[exempt](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/st/transactions_not_subject_to_sales_tax.htm) from sales tax. Groceries and food for home consumption are not taxed. If you make a purchase from a government agency or tax-exempt organization, you will not be charged sales tax.


There is a third category of goods and services that are not taxable at the state level but may be taxable at the local level. For example, clothing and footwear under $110 per item or pair are exempt from the 4% state tax, but local treatment varies because cities/counties can choose whether to adopt the exemption.


In New York City, beautician services, hair restoration, tanning, nail services, massage, weight loss clinics, and credit rating services are all subject to New York City’s local sales tax.


Category Generally Taxable? Notes


**Tangible personal property** Yes Most physical goods are taxable unless specifically exempt


**Groceries** No Food for home consumption is generally exempt


**Clothing** Varies Items under $110 are exempt from state sales tax but may be taxed locally


**Nonprescription drugs** No


**Prescription drugs** No


**SaaS** Varies Prewritten software is taxable; custom software is generally not taxable


**Hotel rooms/short-term rentals** Yes New York City also imposes an occupancy tax


**Educational services** No


**Restaurant food and beverage sales** Yes


### What is subject to sales tax in New York


- Furniture, appliances, and light fixtures
- Motor vehicles, boats, and yachts
- Certain clothing and footwear
- Candy and confections
- Bottled water
- Soda, beer, and alcohol
- Cigarettes and tobacco products
- Animals (pets, livestock not bought for farm production)
- Trees, shrubs, flowers (nursery stock not bought for farm production)
- Restaurant food and drinks


### What’s exempt from sales tax in New York


- Clothing and footwear under $110
- Items for resale
- Capital building improvements
- Prescriptions and non-prescription medication
- Medical equipment and prosthetics
- Feminine hygiene products
- Property and services used for farming or commercial horse boarding
- Sales by funeral homes


### SaaS and digital goods taxability in New York


[Prewritten software is taxable in New York](https://www.numeral.com/blog/saas-sales-tax-new-york) , even if it is delivered electronically or accessed remotely. Custom software is generally not taxable.


### Resale and exemption certificates in New York


To purchase items for resale, a business owner must have a[sales tax exemption certificate](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/tg_bulletins/st/exemption_certificates_for_sales_tax.htm) . This certificate is[Form ST-120](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/current_forms/st/st120_fill_in.pdf) , Resale Certificate. Before a New York business can file for this certificate, they need a valid Certificate of Authority and its sales tax identification number.


If the business is out of state, they can file Form ST-120 without a New York registration number. They can provide the sales tax registration number from their home state, but they can’t provide an out-of-state resale certificate.


New York also doesn’t accept the Multistate Tax Commission Uniform Sales & Use Tax Resale Certificate or the Streamlined Sales Tax Exemption Certificate.


You should retain resale certificates for at least three years after the due date of the return the certificate relates to, or the date that return was filed, if later. Numeral can[manage all your exemption certificates](https://www.numeral.com/product/exemption-certificate-management) , so you don’t have to.


Certificates don’t expire. As long as you are purchasing from the same seller, you can use a blanket certificate. If your address, identification number, or other information changes, you’ll need to get a new certificate.


## Registering for a New York sales tax license


Anyone who sells taxable property or services in New York[must register](https://www.numeral.com/product/registrations) with the Department of Taxation and Finance.


This includes:


- People who sell out of their homes
- Temporary vendors, even if you only sell once a year
- Online sellers who meet the requirements for economic nexus
- A business that falls under[the 2008 presumption definition](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/st/newpresumptionstvendor.htm) of a sales tax vendor


In 2008, the New York State government passed legislation that created a presumption that certain sellers are sales tax vendors. A business falls under the presumption rule if it:


- Pays New York residents commission for sales or referrals, and
- The value of those sales in New York is more than $10,000 in the preceding four tax quarters.


If your business meets the above[requirements](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/tg_bulletins/st/do_i_need_to_register_for_sales_tax.htm) , you must register as a sales tax vendor by:


- **Creating a**[NY.gov business account](https://www.tax.ny.gov/online/bus.htm) **.** You will need this to access the New York Business Express. (Note: A[NY.gov](http://ny.gov/) individual account will not work.)
- **Gathering all the items on the**[application checklist](https://www.tax.ny.gov/e-services/elcoa/#checklist) **.** You will need your information, such as your business contact information, entity information, the date you will begin business, bank account information, and license numbers.
- **Completing the**[DTF-17.1 Business Contact and Responsible Person Questionnaire](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/current_forms/st/dtf17_1.pdf) .
- **Applying for a**[DTF-17: Certificate of Authority](https://www.tax.ny.gov/e-services/elcoa/) **.**


You must apply for the[Certificate of Authority](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/tg_bulletins/st/how_to_register_for_nys_sales_tax.htm) at least 20 days before you begin sales. There are two types of Certificates of Authority: regular and temporary. The application process is the same. The certificate you use depends on your business.


A regular Certificate of Authority is for businesses that regularly make taxable sales from a home, store, stand, or other location. This also applies to sellers at craft shows, flea markets, and antique shows. Even if you only occasionally sell at these events, you will need the regular Certificate of Authority.


If you intend to make taxable sales in New York for no more than two consecutive sales tax quarters in 12 months, you should apply for a temporary Certificate of Authority. The certificate is only valid for the dates listed.


If your business operates out of multiple locations, you will need a separate certificate for each location. You can use the same sales tax identification number and file a combined return. If you operate multiple businesses, each business must have a separate certificate.


### Registration requirements for remote sellers


Out-of-state sellers must register with the Department of Taxation and Finance when they establish physical or economic nexus. An[out-of-state seller meets economic nexus](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/publications/sales/nexus.htm) when they meet both **** of these requirements in the preceding four sales tax quarters:


- More than $500,000 in gross sales of tangible personal property or taxable services delivered into New York
- More than 100 separate sales of tangible personal property delivered into New York


Once you cross the threshold, you[have 30 days to register](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/publications/sales/nexus.htm) as a sales tax vendor, and you must begin collecting tax 20 days after that. Before you make taxable sales, you must have a Certificate of Authority.


Remote sellers apply for a Certificate of Authority through the New York Business Express. Since New York is not a member of the Streamlined Sales Tax Registration System, business owners cannot use that program.


## Collecting New York sales tax


When you have your business's Certificate of Authority, you can begin to collect sales tax by following these steps:


1. **Determine whether the transaction is taxable** using this[guide](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/tg_bulletins/st/quick_reference_guide_for_taxable_and_exempt_property_and_services.htm) . Most tangible personal property is taxable.
2. **Check for exemptions.** If the property or service is exempt, make sure you have the appropriate tax exemption or resale certificates.
3. **Determine the sourcing location.** New York uses destination-based sourcing, so the sales tax rate depends on where the customer takes delivery.
4. **Apply the correct rate.** Use the[Jurisdiction/Rate Lookup by Address](https://www8.tax.ny.gov/JRLA/jrlaStart) tool to make sure you charge the correct rate for that location. In some tax jurisdictions, you must also charge the 0.375% Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District (MCTD) tax.
5. **Collect the tax** from the customer at the time of sale.
6. **Track your sales.** Keep records of all taxable sales, exempt sales, and the tax you collect in each tax jurisdiction. This will make reporting and filing easier.


### Marketplace sales


Marketplace providers like eBay and Amazon generally collect and remit New York sales tax on the taxable sales that they facilitate. A marketplace provider should provide a seller with[ST-150: Marketplace Provider Certificate of Collection](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pdf/current_forms/st/st150.pdf) .


Instead of this certificate, the marketplace provider can have a[publicly available agreement](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/publications/sales/marketplace.htm) with the marketplace seller that states the provider will collect sales tax on these sales.


If you are selling on a marketplace platform, you are still responsible for tracking those sales and reporting the sales as nontaxable on your New York sales tax returns.


### Shipping and delivery charges


Shipping and delivery are taxable if the underlying product or service is taxable. If the seller lists the shipping or delivery charge separately, it is still taxable. It also applies if the seller personally delivers the order or hires a common carrier.


If a product or service is tax-exempt, then the shipping and delivery charge is generally exempt. This includes purchases with a valid resale or exemption certificate.


If the purchase contains a mix of taxable and exempt items, the single shipping charge is taxable. The seller can also allocate the shipping charge between taxable and exempt items, then apply sales tax to the taxable portion.


[Numeral's shipping tax guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-on-shipping) can help you determine when shipping is taxable.


## Filing and paying New York sales tax


Registered businesses must file sales tax monthly, quarterly, or annually. New York places most new vendors on a quarterly filing schedule to start. This may change later depending on taxable activity or amount of tax due.


Your Online Services account will show the filing frequency and due date.


Filing Frequency General Requirement


**Monthly** Taxable receipts total $300,000 or more during a quarter


**Quarterly** Taxable receipts were less than $300,000 during the previous quarter, unless the state determines that the business should file annually


**Annual** Sales and use tax due is $3,000 or less during the annual filing period, subject to state classification


When your business reaches $300,000 in receipts, you will begin filing monthly in the first month of the next tax quarter. You must submit Form ST-809 for the first two months. Then, you will file Form ST-810 to reconcile the entire quarter.


If your sales drop under $300,000, you will continue filing monthly until your taxable activity stays below that threshold for four consecutive quarters.


Returns are due within 20 days after the reporting period ends. Monthly returns are due on the 20th of the following month. Quarterly returns are due on March 20, June 20, September 20, and December 20. Annual returns cover March 1 through the last day of February and are due on March 20.


If the deadline is on a weekend or holiday, the return is due the next business day. Always check your Online Services Account for the latest notices and guidance.


### Filing New York sales tax online


[To file New York sales tax online](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-new-york-sales-tax-online) , you’ll use the New York Sales Tax Web File with your Business Online Services Account. You can make electronic payments from your bank account using Sales Tax Web File.


When your sales and use tax liability exceeds $500,000, the state will require you to enroll in PrompTax. You generally will make payments on an accelerated schedule.


Marketplace sellers or sellers with no taxable sales must file a tax return during each filing period. Don’t report the marketplace provider’s collected tax as your own tax due.


Business owners will file both state and local taxes on a combined return. However, they must break down taxable activity by local jurisdiction and complete the required local schedules. That’s why accurately tracking sales in each jurisdiction matters.


Certain items and locations may have additional schedules. For example, clothing and fuel may have separate schedules.


Certain transactions and services in New York City, Nassau County, and Niagara County require separate schedules. This[New York filing guide](https://www.numeral.com/blog/how-to-file-new-york-sales-tax-online) can help you file taxes accurately.


## New York sales tax penalties and interest


New York issues[sales tax penalties](https://www.tax.ny.gov/bus/st/penalties.htm) if you:


- Don’t register to collect tax
- File sales and use tax returns late
- File on time but pay taxes late
- Pay the wrong amount of taxes
- Don’t keep adequate records


Returns filed up to 60 days late are subject to a[penalty](https://www.numeral.com/blog/what-happens-if-you-dont-collect-or-remit-sales-tax) of 10% on the tax due for the first month. For every additional month or partial month you’re late, the state imposes an additional 1% penalty up to 30%.


If you don’t owe tax, the state will still issue a minimum late-filing penalty of $50. If the return is more than 60 days late, the amount may increase.


If you file on time but pay the tax due late, the penalty is also 10% for the first month. It increases by 1% for each additional partial or full month. Interest will accrue on unpaid taxes.


## New York sales tax recordkeeping and audits


Keep complete records of every invoice, receipt, sales record, exemption certificate, returns, and tax payments. Your records should show each transaction’s sales tax rate and amount.


If you’re a marketplace seller, you should also keep records of these transactions and your Form ST-150 certificates.


You should plan on keeping your records for three years from the due date of the return to which those records relate, or the date the return is filed, if later.


If you are subject to[an audit](https://www.numeral.com/blog/sales-tax-audit) or legal proceeding, you may need to keep your records even longer, according to[New York’s recordkeeping requirements](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pubs_and_bulls/tg_bulletins/st/record-keeping_requirements_for_sales_tax_vendors.htm) .

## New York sales tax FAQs


**What is the sales tax rate in New York?** The base statewide sales tax rate is 4%. Each local tax jurisdiction applies a local tax. New York City and several surrounding counties also apply an MCTD tax of 0.375%. This can raise the total combined tax rate up to 8.875%.


**What is the economic nexus threshold in New York?** An out-of-state business must meet both of these requirements. It must have over $500,000 in gross sales during the preceding four sales tax quarters. It also must have more than 100 sales of tangible personal property in the same timeframe.


**What services are taxable in New York City?** New York City taxes services like parking, credit reporting, hair and beauty services, tanning, nail services, massage, and gym memberships.


**Are clothing and shoes taxable in New York?** It varies. Clothing and shoes with a price tag of less than $110 per item or pair are exempt from the base sales tax rate. Some tax jurisdictions may require businesses to charge their local tax rate.


**I occasionally sell items at a craft fair, flea market, or antique market. Do I have to register as a sales tax vendor?** Yes, even if you only sell items occasionally, you must register as a sales tax vendor and obtain a regular Certificate of Authority. The temporary Certificate of Authority is not applicable to these sellers. New York no longer has a separate Certificate of Authority for craft and flea market vendors.


**I have a NY.gov Individual Account. Can I use that for my business?** No, you must create a separate[NY.gov business account](https://www.tax.ny.gov/online/bus.htm) to access the New York Business Express and apply for a Certificate of Authority.


**Is SaaS taxable in New York?** Prewritten software, including SaaS, is generally taxable even if the customer accesses it online. Custom software may be exempt.


**I sell on a marketplace provider that submits sales tax on my behalf. Do I still have to file state tax returns?** Yes, if you are registered in New York, you must continue filing returns and report marketplace sales even if they are nontaxable. If you don’t file returns, the state may impose a penalty of $50.
